KHA-10.body:
## Resolution

The owner settled the product choices in the conversation and then delegated the remaining routine defaults rather than approving each detail separately. The defaults below complete that contract. They are specification decisions, not claims that an adapter or live model has passed testing. Later lifecycle choices in [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle) govern Undo and continuously running chess clocks. Throughout this resolution, a technical/capacity/formatting pause means stopped generation or waiting for recovery; it does not freeze the active chess clock.

### Independent chess choices and authoritative state

The model chooses its own move from the position. Do not supply a legal-move list, an enumeration of legal moves in an output schema, engine evaluations, ranked choices, or a replacement move.

One application match controller owns the authoritative position and the result. Its chess-rules component validates and applies moves; it never chooses one for the model. [Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries) will place that controller in the chosen architecture.

Determine whether a position is already terminal before requesting a move. A terminal position is handled by the match lifecycle, not reported as a model failure.

### Position and conversation input

Each move request supplies the current FEN, a readable piece-and-square list, the model's color, whose turn it is, and the fresh clock snapshot required by [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle). These describe the same authoritative snapshot, including castling rights, en passant state, and FEN counters. Derived check status may be stated as a fact; no tactical recommendation is supplied.

For ordinary play and ordinary model switches, send the complete retained match conversation as an attributed full-text transcript. The explicit Undo exception in the lifecycle decision excludes discarded continuations from model input while preserving them in the separate archive. Include prior instructions, game inputs, chosen and rejected replies, complete returned plans, textual reasoning and summaries, correction messages, and actual tool-call/result records if any have arrived. Record original roles, field/block order where exposed, sequence, and requested/returned model identifiers. Distinguish proposed moves from accepted moves. The new model may continue or replace the earlier plan. Include all received candidate choices as attributed history even though only choice zero can act.

Use a losslessly escaped transcript inside ordinary user text, followed by the current move request. Current application rules remain in the system instruction. Historical text stays labeled as historical data rather than becoming a new system instruction. Preserve unknown conversation fields and received opaque values in their exact serialized form as labeled data; do not invent native signatures or replay foreign encrypted state as if it belonged to the destination model. Never infer a move from those fields or execute a historical tool call.

Keep the exact received response or ordered SSE events alongside the logical conversation. This specifies what must be preserved, not how long it survives refresh or where it is stored. Persistence and credential boundaries remain with the lifecycle and architecture tickets. The normal chess contract requests text only. Preserve and pause on an unexpected content type that cannot be completely represented; do not silently discard it.

The app cannot recover unreturned private reasoning, or native data already dropped by proxy translation. See [Determine how conversation history transfers between model families](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-18/determine-how-conversation-history-transfers-between-model-families). A text transcript is the selected portable representation, not a claim of unchanged native reasoning state.

### Proxy request and requested reply

Use ordinary `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the selected advertised routing ID and `stream: true`. Request JSON through the instructions. The baseline sends no tools, forced tool choice, legal-move enum, native conversation-continuation ID, or required provider-specific schema option. Do not depend on a universal sampling or output-token setting.

The logical body is:

```json
{
  "model": "<selected routing ID>",
  "stream": true,
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"<game rules, move/reply contract, and historical-data instructions>"},
    {"role":"user","content":"<complete escaped, attributed transcript>"},
    {"role":"user","content":"<current FEN, piece list, model color, side to move, current clock snapshot/time control, and request for one move>"}
  ]
}
```

This is a request template. It contains no secret. The concrete prompt must say that the model chooses independently, errors receive rule-specific correction, and an optional plan is a brief shareable strategy note.

A move reply requests a JSON object with required `move` and optional `plan` strings:

```json
{"move":"e2e4","plan":"Control the center and develop my pieces."}
```

An explicit resignation can instead be `{"resign":true}`. A missing optional plan is acceptable. Preserve separately returned reasoning as conversation data.

The source-backed adapter limits and ordinary route are documented in [Document CLIProxyAPI model discovery and move requests](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-7/document-cliproxyapi-model-discovery-and-move-requests). No source review establishes universal JSON enforcement or successful chess play.

### Move notation and parsing defaults

Use four-square-character coordinate notation with an optional lowercase promotion suffix, equivalent to `^[a-h][1-8][a-h][1-8][qrbn]?$`. Normalize surrounding whitespace and letter case. Examples include `e2e4` and `e7e8q`.

Represent castling by the king's origin and destination, such as `e1g1`; represent en passant by the moving pawn's origin and destination. Promotion must identify queen, rook, bishop, or knight. The app never chooses a promotion piece for the model.

Only the completed answer content of choice zero can propose a move. Do not select a move from reasoning, the optional plan, other choices, historical messages, or a list of alternatives.

First parse one complete JSON object, optionally enclosed in one Markdown code fence. Conflicting duplicate move keys, incompatible move/resignation declarations, and multiple competing answers require clarification. Extra non-action fields do not invalidate an otherwise unambiguous move; retain them.

If JSON parsing fails, accept a standalone coordinate move or an explicit final `Move: e2e4` line. Permit harmless surrounding whitespace, backticks, and terminal punctuation. Narrative candidate moves are not commands. Multiple explicit selections with different coordinates remain ambiguous. Do not repair JSON or pick a candidate by chess evaluation.

A missing, ambiguous, or syntactically unreadable move is a formatting failure. Missing promotion information is a formatting clarification, not permission to choose a queen. An unambiguously selected coordinate move that violates the current chess rules is an illegal chess attempt, whatever its container.

### Completion and streaming

Accumulate answer text, reasoning fields, and indexed tool-call fields independently, preserving event order in the archive. Do not apply any partial streamed move.

An actionable answer requires a completed response with `finish_reason: "stop"` and no reported stream/request error. For the selected Chat streaming protocol, require normal stream termination as well; `[DONE]` by itself is insufficient. A completed non-streaming fixture must pass the equivalent checks.

A lost stream, truncation, malformed protocol response, provider filter event without an explicit model-authored refusal, or unexpected tool-call finish is a technical interruption. Keep partial content marked incomplete; it cannot move the board or trigger a chess loss. A normally completed answer with no identifiable move or refusal is instead a formatting failure.

No tools are declared or executed. Preserve unexpected tool requests and pause with an unsupported-response explanation. The application does not fabricate tool results.

### Chess corrections and result

Explain the specific violation, such as "That leaves your king in check," and ask the model to choose again. Preserve the unchanged position, rejected reply, and correction in the full conversation. Do not suggest legal replacements.

Allow the initial illegal attempt plus three automatic chess-correction retries, for at most four illegal attempts on the pending chess turn. These are per-turn counters for the model-controlled side. They survive technical recovery and ordinary model switches, and reset when a legal move advances the game. Each attempt retains its producing-model attribution; the match result is not a per-model strength rating.

The fourth illegal attempt is a loss for the model-controlled side. Stop automatic generation and record the reason as exhausted illegal-move attempts.

### Formatting recovery

Formatting failures consume none of the chess-attempt budget and cause no chess loss.

Allow at most three automatic formatting-correction requests on the pending turn, independently of chess corrections. Formatting recovery does not reset illegal-attempt counts. Each completed response is classified once, so a recovered illegal move consumes a chess attempt rather than also consuming another formatting failure.

After the formatting budget is spent, pause with Retry or Switch model. A player-triggered Retry authorizes one additional request; it does not silently refill the automatic formatting budget or erase chess attempts. A player-triggered switch also preserves spent turn budgets. A legal accepted move resets the next turn's budgets.

### Refusal and resignation

An explicit model refusal to make a move counts as resignation and a model loss immediately. Do not spend correction retries trying to reverse it.

Accept `{"resign":true}`, an unambiguous final "I resign" statement, or an explicit final model-authored refusal to move in a complete reply. Quoted, hypothetical, or historical refusal text does not resign. A reply that simultaneously chooses a move and refuses it needs clarification. An unrecognized or ambiguous statement goes through formatting recovery rather than a guessed loss.

An HTTP error, missing response, timeout, provider error object, or filter finish reason alone is not a model resignation. Retain a distinct result reason for resignation and for exhausted illegal attempts.

### Connection errors, waiting, and cancellation defaults

Connection failures, proxy/auth/quota errors, transport timeouts, and incomplete responses stop generation at the unchanged position without an immediate chess loss or spent correction attempt. The active chess clock continues, and its expiry can independently end the match on time under the lifecycle decision. Show the returned error in understandable terms and offer Retry or Switch model. Authentication/configuration failures may also link back to connection settings. Respect a known retry-after period when offering Retry.

Do not add automatic network-generation retries on top of the player's proxy retries. A manual Retry sends one new logical request for the pending turn and preserves the full transcript and spent counters.

Show elapsed waiting status and the live chess clock. The lifecycle decision supersedes the original unlimited-wait default: the active side's clock continues through technical errors, retries, capacity/formatting recovery, Stop request, Undo, queued switches, refresh, and page/device absence. Chess-clock expiry can end a pending turn and fences late replies. A browser/proxy/upstream timeout remains a technical interruption, not itself a resignation or illegal attempt. Do not impose an additional arbitrary generation deadline.

Offer an explicit Stop request action that abandons the pending response and fences late replies without an immediate loss. It stops generation but does not stop the active chess clock or prevent a later time loss. Switching models alone does not stop it. Upstream work may continue after disconnect; do not promise immediate cancellation or a quota refund.

### Model switches and stale-response protection

Let the active response finish before applying a queued switch. Handle that response under its original model identity. Apply any valid move once, or record its refusal/error/illegal attempt, before starting another request. The queued model handles the next generation request, including a needed correction after a completed old-model reply. The authoritative board never changes merely because the selection changed.

If the old reply ends the match through resignation or the fourth illegal attempt, preserve that final loss. A queued selection must not automatically start practice or erase the result.

Associate each request with the game ID, position revision, side to move, conversation segment, and active request generation. Commit a legal move only if all still match and that generation has not already been handled. Increment the position revision with every accepted move. A repeated FEN is not sufficient identity. Duplicate, stale, canceled, or superseded replies are archived with their status and cannot apply a move, increment attempts, or replace a result twice.

Do not start a second actionable generation for the same pending turn while the first is still active. After a failed switch, keep the actual prior selection/position intact and show the candidate's error. The player chooses Retry, another candidate, or explicit resumption with the prior model. No silent model substitution.

### Complete-history capacity

Submit the complete transcript and current request. When destination capacity is known, budget the actual representation plus instructions, current state, and output/reasoning headroom. Unknown catalog limits are not proof of fit, and a previous short check does not certify later turns.

On full-history rejection or known unsupported history/content, pause with a capacity/compatibility explanation and Retry or Choose another model. Preserve the full transcript. Do not trim, summarize, silently drop returned reasoning, reset context, change models automatically, or count it as a chess loss. If no chosen route can accept it, generation remains blocked while the active chess clock continues; clock expiry can independently end the match.

Require synthetic and later authorized live evidence for the actual adapter/configuration. A successful HTTP response cannot prove an upstream never truncates or that a model attends to every token. Do not label that uncertainty as verified full-history support.

### Results, practice, and custom starts

A recorded model loss stays final. If the board is still playable, offer unscored practice continuation using either the same or a new model, with fresh model context containing the usual instructions and current FEN/piece list. Start a distinct practice segment with fresh attempt budgets; preserve the original result and transcript.

Fresh model context does not erase the actual chess position, special-move rights, counters, or the app's known game-state history. Keep that rules state so the continuation is judged from the real position. Earlier model conversation is not sent to the fresh segment. Once the segment starts, ordinary switches transfer its complete conversation.

Any unfinished game can continue with a new model. The match lifecycle owns persistence and resuming interrupted games. Terminal boards cannot generate another move.

A deliberately edited position instead starts a separate labeled game with its own result and fresh context under [Define custom starting positions and position editor](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-19/define-custom-starting-positions-and-position-editor). Its repetition history starts at that custom start.

### Compatibility-check profile and verification

Use a short diagnostic outside scored play to verify the same Chat protocol, transcript envelope, response completion, coordinate parsing, and optional-plan handling. Include a synthetic prior plan with a unique marker and ask for that marker in the returned plan alongside a fixed coordinate-format example. Do not grade chess legality, playing strength, or a model's initial move in this diagnostic. A formatting correction may use the same bounded format-recovery rules. A diagnostic failure blocks match start while keeping the advertised model visible with Retry or Choose another model.

Keep diagnostic records distinct from chess attempts. Any match-associated diagnostic sent during an existing game remains a tagged conversation record. The catalog decision owns when to run checks for switch candidates, refresh, and stale route changes, using this profile.

Required later checks include:

- Deterministic parser fixtures for clean/fenced JSON, clear fallback moves, conflicting answers, duplicate keys, hypothetical moves, promotion choices/missing suffixes, refusal text versus quoted refusal, and separate reasoning fields.
- Chess-rule fixtures for legal/illegal moves, castling, en passant, underpromotion, king safety, the fourth illegal attempt, independent format budgets, manual Retry, and terminal-position prechecks.
- Stream/transport fixtures for fragmented deltas, missing completion, truncation, late/duplicate output, explicit Stop, proxy errors, and a queued switch around each result.
- Lossless full-history fixtures and adapter checks against the pinned CLIProxyAPI baseline, including all returned textual fields and opaque/unknown records. Test ordinary switches, practice resets, custom starts, and rejected full-history input.
- Authorized live checks of actually available GPT/Codex, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, and unknown/custom routes before asserting their observed compatibility. Record route/proxy version, actual payload, and limits. Do not claim coverage for routes not exercised.

No new generation requests or product tests were run to settle this decision. The existing research supplies source constraints and its own explicitly recorded offline tests. This resolution specifies later acceptance work, not results from that work.

### Later lifecycle decision: explicit Undo exception

The owner subsequently approved same-match undo with the discarded moves removed from future model context in [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle). That ticket owns the undo behavior. For subsequent generation and ordinary model switches, "complete conversation" means the complete retained line after undo. Keep discarded received records in the separate archive; do not replay them, summarize them into the prompt, or reuse provider continuation state that carries them. This explicit player action is not silent compaction or a capacity-recovery shortcut. Recorded final losses remain final, and stale-response fencing still applies after restoring an earlier board.

### Later lifecycle decision: timed play

The owner chose timed matches, model awareness of remaining time, and clocks that keep running regardless of page closure in [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle). That ticket owns time controls, continuously running clock operation, expiry results, saved-game reconciliation, Undo without time refunds, and fresh timed practice segments. Its latest no-clock-pause policy supersedes the earlier proposed technical-error pause. Errors do not themselves cause chess losses, but the active clock can expire while recovery is blocked. Every move/correction request includes a fresh snapshot of both sides' remaining time and the time control. This is request-time awareness, not a continuous update during one response.

KHA-11.body:
## Resolution

The owner chose guest autosaves plus optional account sync, same-match Undo that removes the discarded continuation from model context, timed matches with model clock awareness, and a clock that keeps running regardless of leaving the page. The remaining routine defaults below use the owner's standing delegation. This is a product specification, not a claim that a website, chess library, clock service, or live model has been tested.

### Starting a match

Support orthodox chess. Before Start game, the human chooses White, Black, or Random, an advertised model under [Choose the model catalog and opponent selection rules](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-9/choose-the-model-catalog-and-opponent-selection-rules), and a time control. Default to White and 15 minutes per side plus a 10-second increment. Starting minutes must be positive; increment may be zero. Let the player change these settings before starting. MVP games are timed.

Complete connection setup and the required model compatibility check before starting either clock or creating an active game. A failed check leaves setup open. Never spend a player's clock on a pre-game diagnostic.

A normal game starts from the normal position with White to move. A custom-position game follows [Define custom starting positions and position editor](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-19/define-custom-starting-positions-and-position-editor), including its FEN settings, counters, fresh model context, and separate result. The declared side to move determines which clock starts. Do not request a move from an already terminal position.

Start game fixes the initial position, colors, and time control for that game and starts the side-to-move clock. If that side is the model, begin one move request. Changing those setup settings later creates a new game rather than silently rewriting the active one.

### Turns and chess rules

Only the side to move can play. Human illegal board input is rejected without changing the position or stopping the clock; the model's four-illegal-attempt rule does not apply to human input. Human promotion requires a choice of queen, rook, bishop, or knight. The clock runs while that choice is open.

Support king safety, castling, en passant, and promotion, including underpromotion. The application applies only validated moves and checks for an ending after each accepted move. The model remains responsible for choosing its own moves under [Define legal move selection and model failure behavior](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-10/define-legal-move-selection-and-model-failure-behavior).

The casual-play default is automatic draws for stalemate, a dead position where neither side can ever checkmate by a legal sequence, threefold repetition, or 100 half-moves without a pawn move or capture. The threefold and fifty-move thresholds are applied automatically for either side rather than requiring a human claim or a new model draw-claim command. This is a deliberate simplification of claim procedures. Checkmate on the just-accepted move takes precedence over a move-count draw. The architecture ticket must verify actual library support and expose gaps instead of treating a coarse material check as proof of all dead positions. Negotiated draw offers are outside this MVP lifecycle.

Custom starts keep imported half-move counters and begin repetition history at the custom start. A terminal imported setup remains editable, with Start game disabled and an explanation. Do not invent earlier repetition history or normalize counters to make the position playable.

### Clocks run continuously

Only the side to move's clock runs. The other side's clock is stopped until a legal accepted move transfers the turn. Add the configured increment once after a legal accepted move. Rejected, partial, duplicated, canceled, or stale moves earn no increment.

The owner's latest choice supersedes the earlier proposed technical-error clock pause. While a game is unfinished, its active clock keeps running through thinking, streaming, illegal-move and formatting corrections, network/provider errors, rate limits, waiting for Retry, capacity problems, model-switch checks, Stop request, Undo, page navigation, tab closure, browser/device suspension, sign-in, and cross-device handoff. There is no Pause game action. Only an accepted move transfers the running clock; a final result stops it.

A generation interruption leaves the board waiting for recovery, but the chess clock remains live. An HTTP/provider timeout, quota error, or incomplete reply is not itself a resignation, illegal attempt, or immediate loss. The side can nevertheless lose later because its chess clock reaches zero before an accepted legal move. Retry and model switching neither reset nor refill it. Respect retry-after without freezing the clock. A queued model switch still lets the old response finish, except that clock expiry or an explicit Stop/Undo can make that response ineligible.

When the active clock expires, settle one time result and stop actionable generation. The expired side loses on time unless the opponent cannot possibly checkmate from that position through any legal sequence, in which case the result is a draw. The rules dependency must support this position-sensitive distinction; a generic total-material heuristic is not sufficient evidence. A late completed move or early partial move cannot reverse an expired result. The controller must serialize accepted moves, endings, clock expiry, and Undo against one authoritative event order and resolve boundary cases exactly once.

Store remaining time and an elapsed-time reference/deadline, not only the last displayed numbers. Reconstruct elapsed time while a page/device is absent; a suspended JavaScript timer must not freeze the game. On reopening or another device's takeover, reconcile clock expiry before enabling a move, Retry, Undo, or a new model request. If it expired during the absence, record the result at that expiry rather than giving fresh time at reopening.

Clock continuity does not promise that browser-side model generation continues after a tab closes. Only a response actually accepted by the authoritative controller can transfer the turn. An abandoned browser request does not become a move retrospectively. The architecture must verify the chosen timing authority, closed-tab behavior, device sleep, time-source changes, and cross-device ordering without silently moving proxy credentials or generation onto the website's server.

### Model awareness of time

Every move-generation request, including correction requests and manual retries, includes a fresh authoritative snapshot taken just before dispatch. State the model's color, its remaining time in clear units, the human side's remaining time, the selected time control and increment, and which clock is running. Supply this alongside the canonical current FEN and readable piece list.

Label older clock readings in the retained conversation as historical. Instruct the model to finish its independently chosen move within its current remaining time. Do not send a legal-move list or change the independent-move contract to make it faster.

The model sees the snapshot at request time. It does not receive continuous clock updates during one response. Every later request gets a new snapshot. Do not send timer-tick prompts, parallel turn requests, hidden context resets, or provider-native conversation continuations to simulate live clock updates. Prompting the model about time does not guarantee that it responds before expiry.

### Undo in the same match

The owner approved Undo within the existing match and requested that the model forget the undone move. The routine default is one full human decision: return to the previous human turn, taking back the human move and any model reply after it. If a model request is still pending, abandon it before restoring the checkpoint. Repeated Undo can reach earlier human decision points, but not before the game's start or across a fresh-context practice boundary. Before the human has had any decision point, Undo is unavailable.

Restore the checkpoint's position, side to move, castling/en passant rights, move counters, known repetition history, turn recovery budgets, and opponent selection. Discard queued selection changes in the undone continuation. This is an explicit board/history takeback, not a separate Reset retries action.

Restore the corresponding retained match conversation as well. Exclude undone moves, replies, plans/reasoning, corrections, later diagnostics, and any later message revealing that continuation from future model requests. Do not tell the model what was undone or append a summary of it. Use stateless requests constructed from the retained history rather than a provider continuation identifier that could retain discarded turns. Ordinary model switches after Undo carry the complete retained line.

Keep discarded received records in a separate attributed match archive, outside future model context. This preserves the lossless received-data requirement while making Undo an explicit exception to replaying every previously received message. The app cannot erase records already held by the proxy/provider or guarantee deletion from their systems.

Undo does not refund elapsed clock time or restore the old clock readings. Charge the previously active side up to the accepted Undo event, remove increment credits earned only by the undone moves, and start the restored side-to-move clock from its resulting current bank. If removing those credits would leave either side without positive time, reject Undo without changing the position or clocks and explain the reason. This prevents repeated takebacks from manufacturing increment time. Reconcile an already expired clock first; Undo cannot erase a time result.

Invalidate in-flight requests and advance live request/position versions even when the board returns to an earlier FEN. Late replies from the discarded line cannot apply moves, consume attempts, add increment, or replace a result. Persist/sync the new current line so a stale tab or device cannot resurrect the discarded continuation.

An already recorded final result remains final. Undo applies only to an unfinished game or unfinished practice segment; Undo in practice never changes the original result. Playing an earlier position after a finalized game uses a separate custom-position game.

### Saving, accounts, and recovery

Guest play requires no account. Automatically save the full game in the same browser so refresh, navigation, and reopening can recover it. Browser data deletion/eviction can remove guest saves; show save failures rather than claiming a game is durably saved when it is not.

Optional accounts add cross-device game access and automatic synchronization for account-associated games. Keep a local copy for interrupted connectivity and sync pending changes when possible. Offer to add existing guest games to the signed-in account rather than silently merging unrelated games. Preserve identities, results, and current-line/archived-line distinctions during import. Signing in, signing out, syncing, and importing do not pause clocks or reset time. Private account games are accessible only to their owner.

Save the initial position, current rules state, accepted move history and repetition history, time control and clock references, model attributions and current/queued selections, request/position versions, spent turn budgets, complete retained conversation, separate received-data archive, final result/reason, and any practice segment. FEN alone cannot resume this contract. Account games remain available until their owner deletes them under the eventual data policy; implementation and storage limits must be addressed in architecture rather than silently dropping conversation history.

Support one authoritative writer per game across tabs/devices. Handoff or recovery must fence the earlier writer and its responses, preserve the live deadlines, and reject stale overwrites. An offline account copy cannot silently replace a newer accepted line or final result. The architecture must define the concrete ownership and conflict mechanism.

Reopening restores the game and reconciles elapsed time before play. Do not blindly repeat an in-flight request after refresh or handoff. Establish whether it is still actionable, fence it if abandoned, and offer explicit Retry or a model switch at the unchanged position when needed. The clock continues throughout this recovery. Any unfinished, unexpired game can continue with the same model or a newly selected model under the ordinary full-retained-history rule.

Proxy endpoints, credentials, storage/retention, and cross-device connection setup remain governed by [Choose supported proxy setups and credential handling](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-8/choose-supported-proxy-setups-and-credential-handling). Account sync is not permission to store proxy keys on the website's server. A second device may need its own supported route to the player's proxy.

### Endings and new games

Record win/loss/draw, side, and reason distinctly: checkmate, human resignation, model resignation, exhausted model illegal attempts, time loss, or the specific draw rule. A human may resign an unfinished game. Resolve any earlier authoritative clock expiry first. Starting another game, leaving, or disconnecting is not an implicit resignation or pause.

Preserve the agreed immediate model loss after an explicit refusal and the fourth illegal attempt. A technical error alone causes neither. A time loss is a separate reason. Results are final once recorded, and no stale response, retry, queued switch, Undo, or sync conflict may rewrite them.

New game/Restart opens setup and creates a separate game with fresh clocks and context after Start. The old game's history/result is preserved; an unfinished old game keeps its clock running unless it is explicitly resigned or otherwise ends. Do not implement Restart by erasing an existing match. Rematch also creates a new game, initially reusing the prior starting position, model, and time control with human colors swapped; allow setup changes before Start.

After a model loss on a still-playable board, offer the agreed explicit unscored practice continuation with the same or another model. Extend this to a model time loss as well as resignation/illegal-attempt loss. Preserve the original result and archive. Start a separate practice segment with fresh conversation and turn budgets, the actual retained rules/repetition state, and fresh clocks under the chosen time control. Its clocks begin only on Start practice and then obey the same continuous-time rules. Ordinary switches within practice carry that segment's full retained conversation. A practice ending never adds a new scored result to the original game.

A checkmated, stalemated, or otherwise terminal board cannot generate another move. Editing it starts a separate labeled custom-position game under the existing custom-start decision. That differs from unscored continuation of the unchanged playable board after a model loss.

### Required downstream verification

[Validate the connection and chess match interface](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-12/validate-the-connection-and-chess-match-interface) must cover setup/color/promotion, both live clocks, time-control selection, recovery with the clock still running, Undo and its context boundary, guest saves/account access, expired saved games, rematch, and distinct final/practice states on desktop/mobile.

[Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries) must verify continuous clock authority with all clients closed, elapsed-time recovery, one-writer handoff, account ownership/storage, full archive/current-line separation, and the selected library's exact draw/timeout-mating rules. It owns the authentication mechanism, timer/state placement, background-processing limits, and reliable storage design.

[Agree on MVP acceptance criteria and the specification handoff](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-14/agree-on-mvp-acceptance-criteria-and-the-specification-handoff) must require evidence for clock expiry during thinking/retries/errors/closed tabs, boundary races and late responses, fresh clock snapshots on every request, promotion under time, Undo without time refunds or increment farming, branch-safe context replay and sync, guest/account resumption, interrupted requests, final-result preservation, draw rules, and practice clocks. Verify imported counters and retained versus reset repetition history.

No production implementation, model requests, browser prototype, or live compatibility checks were performed to settle this ticket. These requirements must be verified on the eventual implementation. No additional decision ticket is needed for these lifecycle defaults; remaining connectivity, model-selection, interface, architecture, and final acceptance questions remain in their existing tickets.

KHA-19.body:
## Resolution

### Custom starting positions

The MVP will let human players set their own starting positions for play against a model opponent. Chess.com and Lichess were cited as familiar examples.

### Input methods

Support both a visual board editor where players arrange pieces and FEN import by pasting a position string.

### Position validation

Allow free editing of the setup, but block starting play until the position passes basic chess-validity checks. Invalid setups, such as a missing king or adjacent kings, must be corrected before play begins.

Check the current board and position settings for consistency. Do not require proof of a complete legal move history from the normal starting position.

Basic validation covers the input structure and field values, king placement, pawn ranks, side-to-move/check consistency, and declared castling/en passant state. Rejections must identify the failed check and affected setting or square so the player can correct it.

This is setup validation. It does not supply legal moves or strategic advice to the model.

### Position settings

The visual editor includes controls for the side to move, castling rights, and en passant state. Populate these settings automatically from imported FEN.

These settings are part of the starting position and must agree with the position used for play and supplied to the model.

### Custom-start results

A game started from a custom position records its own win, loss, or draw result and is labeled "Custom position."

Post-loss practice continuation remains unscored under the accepted decisions in [Define legal move selection and model failure behavior](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-10/define-legal-move-selection-and-model-failure-behavior).

### Editing a position from an existing game

Starting play from an edited position creates a separate custom-position game. Preserve the original game and any recorded result.

The new game follows the custom-start result policy above and starts with fresh model context as specified below.

### Starting model context

A new custom-position game starts with fresh model context containing the usual game instructions, the starting FEN, and the readable piece list. Leave any source game's conversation with that original game.

This fresh start applies to new custom-position games. Ordinary mid-game model switches still carry that game's full prior conversation under [Define legal move selection and model failure behavior](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-10/define-legal-move-selection-and-model-failure-behavior).

### Move counters and repetition history

Preserve the imported FEN's move number and fifty-move-rule counter. Count repeated positions only from the new custom-position game's start.

Do not invent earlier position history or carry the source game's repetition record into the separate custom-position game. These game-state rules are distinct from the fresh model conversation.

### Terminal starting positions

Allow checkmate and stalemate positions to remain viewable and editable. Disable Start game and clearly explain that the position is already terminal.

### Verification and downstream work

This resolves the product choices for custom starting positions. It does not claim that a chess library or prototype has passed these checks.

[Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries) must verify the chosen chess library's current-position validation, FEN state preservation, and terminal-position detection against this boundary.

[Validate the connection and chess match interface](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-12/validate-the-connection-and-chess-match-interface) covers the editor, FEN import, actionable errors, and disabled Start game state. [Agree on MVP acceptance criteria and the specification handoff](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-14/agree-on-mvp-acceptance-criteria-and-the-specification-handoff) must include these scenarios and distinguish source facts from observed behavior.

Draw adjudication and resumption of existing games remain in [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle).

KHA-12.body:
## Resolution

The owner reviewed the prototype and chose A, Classic workspace: "yeah let's go with A".

Use A's conventional board with player rows/clocks and the right-hand opponent, moves, and conversation panel as the implementation reference. Keep the normal Chess.com layout direction with T3 Code styling and its actual selectable themes. Seasonal Halloween bot presentation remains excluded. B and C remain archived alternatives on the throwaway branch.

Complete screen-reader play alongside keyboard, mouse, and touch remains required, including named squares/pieces, keyboard move selection, explicit accessible promotion, focus restoration, and concise turn/error announcements. Preserve the previously resolved connection, model-selection, full-history, queued-switch/recovery, continuously running clock, Undo, and immutable-result policies.

Primary source: `prototype/match-interface`, commit `6af7fa61aec5668b4e8b42c1f1ba4a89f37cda45`, with the portable bundle attached to this issue as `5016386e-694c-4203-8789-fe37e513feff`. The earlier prototype-ready comment records the verified checksum and run instructions.

This resolves the interface choice and interaction/input scope. It does not establish production implementation, a stack/license choice, live model compatibility, native browser/device support, or completed assistive-technology acceptance. Those remain architecture and acceptance work. Keep the throwaway code off main.

Carry the approved A reference into [Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries) and [Agree on MVP acceptance criteria and the specification handoff](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-14/agree-on-mvp-acceptance-criteria-and-the-specification-handoff).
